newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean fund manager in Mexican deal talks.
newsitem.headline: Chilean fund manager in Mexican deal talks.

text.p: Chilean pension fund manager Habitat SA said it is in talks with Mexican financial group Grupo Serfin to set up an administrator to take part in Mexico's new private pension system which will start in 1997.
"The union could be agreed in the next few weeks," vice president Ricardo Zabala told a news conference.
Serfin will own 51 percent of the new fund manager with the rest held by a Chilean company set up this year by Habitat and Citibank, he said.
The firms will invest between $80 million and $100 million and aim to capture a 20 percent market share, the maximum limit allowed by Mexican law, said Zabala.
Habitat is the latest in a stream of Chilean pension funds forging deals to take part in Mexico's private pension system which was modelled on Chile's own free-market scheme.
Chile's largest fund manager Provida has linked up with Grupo Provincial de Mexico while Santa Maria has signed a deal with Bancomer.
